pages.en:
POLICE FORCE,
MUNICIPAL COUNCIL.
Shanghai, 2.8. 1932
To. J.C. (Online)

Encloses statement & copy
of British Subject. L.S. Bentley
& passed for information.
He states he is going
to H.B.M. Consul this morning
to report the matter.
Bentley served a sentence
of 3 months imprisonment for
Trafficking in Arms. Sentenced
in the British Court 21.3.28
Released on Remission 8.6.28
C.R.C No 1712.
Yours Obediently,
J. Dickson
S.I.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Lewis Draper Bentley
native of British Subject taken by me written by himself
at 4.15 p.m. on the 1st Mar. 1932 and interpreted by:

My name is Lewis D. Bentley, British subject, thirty
years of age, an employee of Messrs. Mitsui Bussan Kaisha, in
Coal Delivery Dept. for seven years. On the 15th Feb. 1932,
I was told by my boss to call the three coal lighters No. 7
No.12, No.14, from Toyoda Mill to return to our Pootung Wharf.
Arriving at the mill, I found the boatmen wanted to run away,
because the lighters seals are broken. I told them to stop
on the boat and take them back to our wharf. As No.7 lighter
has three persons, No 12 lighter also three and No.14 lighter
has only two persons, the boatmen called me to help them and
stay on the rudder. So I gave a chit to my motor driver, to
take to office, telling them where I am. Everything went well
for a while, on reaching Sho-so-do, or Ferry Road, in Soochow
Creek, about twenty loafers jumped to the lighters, throw the
anchors and demanded to know what it was. I explained to them
very plainly in Chinese, that its Japanese coal and we are
returning it back to the M.B.K. Wharf, because the boatmen
refused to work for Japanese. So they wanted $50.00 for each
lighter to pass. As I have not enough money on me, I said, I
will give them a chit, to collect the money from our Company.
So they said, you want us to be arrested by the Japanese, so
you are a Japanese citizen, and we will take you to the
Military Headquarters and have you shot. Now I find things are
bad, I agree to go with them to the Military Headquarters. On
the way, they search me and took away my note book, a fountain
pen, an Eveready pencil and two notes of $15.00 (one $5.00 and
one $10.00). Going to Chungshan Road, I saw a Chinese Merchant

警务调查报告。

以下为英籍人士 Lewis Draper Bentley 的陈述，
由本人于1932年3月1日下午4时15分采集，由其亲笔书写，并由……翻译：

我叫 Lewis D. Bentley，英籍人士，
三十岁，在三井物产株式会社（Mitsui Bussan Kaisha）
煤炭配送部工作了七年。1932年2月15日，
我的老板让我去叫三艘运煤驳船，编号7号、
12号、14号，从丰田纱厂返回我们的浦东码头。
到达纱厂后，我发现船夫想逃跑，
因为驳船的封条被破坏了。我让他们留在船上，
并把他们带回我们的码头。由于7号驳船上有三人，
12号驳船上也有三人，而14号驳船上只有两人，
船夫叫我帮忙掌舵。于是我写了一张便条给我的汽车司机，
让他带到办公室，告诉他们我在哪里。起初一切顺利，
当到达苏州河的硕所渡（Sho-so-do），即摆渡路时，
大约二十个无业游民跳上驳船，抛下锚，
质问这是什么情况。我用中文向他们清楚地解释，
这是日本煤炭，我们要把它运回三井物产株式会社的码头，
因为船夫拒绝为日本人工作。于是他们要求每艘驳船
支付50美元才能放行。由于我身上带的钱不够，
我说我会给他们一张便条，让他们向我们要公司收款。
于是他们说，你想让我们被日本人逮捕，所以
你是日本公民，我们要把你带到军事司令部
枪毙你。现在我发现情况不妙，便同意跟他们去军事司令部。
在路上，他们搜了我的身，拿走了我的笔记本、
一支钢笔、一支永备牌（Eveready）铅笔和两张共15美元的钞票
（一张5美元，一张10美元）。走到中山路时，我看到一名中国商团

ters. Reaching a Military Camp at Chungsen Road and Markham
Road Station, the Captain asked the loafers and they accused
me of being an employee of a Japanese firm, and I have
dismissed one of the former boatmen for no reason. The
Captain asked for my name and wrote a petition of their
statement and added that I am a Japanese spy, and sent me
to Chenju to the 78th Division, I was asked again, and this
time, I explained everything. Being an employee of a
Japanese firm, I have to perform my duties as a servant,
and the rest as stated above. So the Chinese police officer
said I was a spy. I told them that I was taken up by a group
of loafers on the lighter in Soochow Creek, and how can I be
a spy when I am working with the Chinese boatmen. The
Military officer told me to stay for a while, and he'll
investigate the matter. About an hour after, he called me
to sleep in the same room with the Quarter-master sergeant
and he said if I can give a shop guarantee, I can go to-morrow.
As I cannot communicate with the people in Shanghai, I stayed
for two days in Chenju and on 17th, they send me to Nanziang
to the 60th Division, and on the 18th, I was sent back to
Chenju, to the Ministry of Communication, at about 8.15 a.m.
and then to Loong-wha, the Military Headquarters, I was asked
again and I told them the same story, then they sent me to the
Mayor of Greater Shanghai. I stayed till 6 p.m. and was
sent to the Nantao Police Station. I remained there till
the 28th, when I was questioned. As I told them again the

以下为....................................................................................................的陈述，
籍贯...............................................................，由本人于........................................在........................................采集，并由....................................翻译。

义勇队员，我叫他跟我一起去军事司令部。
到达真如路和麦根路（Markham Road）车站附近的一个军营，
营长询问那些无业游民，他们指控我是日本公司的雇员，
并且我无故开除了一名之前的船夫。
营长问了我的名字，写下了一份关于他们陈述的请愿书，
并称我是日本间谍，随后将我送到陈菊（Chenju，音译）的第78师。
我再次受到讯问，这次我解释了一切。作为
一家日本公司的雇员，我必须履行仆人的职责，
其余情况如上所述。于是中国警官说我是间谍。
我告诉他们，我是在苏州河的驳船上被一群无业游民抓走的，
既然我和中国船夫一起工作，怎么可能是间谍呢？
那位军官让我稍等片刻，他说他会调查此事。
大约一小时后，他叫我去和军需中士睡在同一间房间里，
并说如果我能提供一家商铺的担保，明天就可以离开。
由于我无法与上海方面的人联系，我在陈菊（Chenju，音译）待了两天，
17日，他们把我送到南翔（Nanziang）的第60师，
18日，我又被送回陈菊（Chenju，音译）的交通部，
大约在上午8点15分，随后又被送到龙华军事司令部。
我再次受到讯问，讲了同样的故事，然后他们把我送到
大上海市长那里。我一直待到下午6点，随后被送到
南市警察局。我一直留在那里直到28日，期间受到讯问。
因为我再次告诉他们
